newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Private capital to emerging markets jumped in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Private capital to emerging markets jumped in 1996.

text.p: Emerging market economies attracted around $230 billion in private capital in 1996 and could attract as much again in 1997, according to a report issued on Saturday.

"Private capital flows to emerging market economies rose 19 percent in 1996 to reach a new high of about $230 billion," the Institute of International Finance said in the report, which was released at the World Economic Forum.
"They are likely to remain at this record level again this year as strong continued growth in equity flows offsets a moderation in borrowing," it said.
Net official flows fell sharply last year, so that total capital flows remained virtually unchanged at the 1995 level of just below $240 billion.
It said private flows would likely plateau in 1997 after the record year in 1996, but special factors were disguising the upward trend.
"In 1997, more moderate flows to a few large countries are likely to offset continued expansion in flows to most emerging market economies," the study said.

It expected equity flows to continue to rise by about 12 percent in 1997, reflecting an increase in both direct and portfolio investment. This would return equity flows to their 50 percent share in total private flows in 1993 to 1996, it said.
